test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-II (Statistics) Official Paper-II (Held On: 19 Jan, 2025)
subject: general
question: What is the main assumption of the ratio-to-moving-averages method?

options.text: Random components dominate the time series.
The trend is constant over time.

solution:
**The Correct Answer is :The seasonal component is additive.**

**Explanation:**

The **ratio-to-moving-averages method** assumes that the time series components combine **multiplicatively**.

In this method:

 
• 
 
Observed value = **Trend × Seasonal × Irregular**

 
 
• 
 
Seasonal indices are obtained by taking **ratios** of actual values to moving averages.

 

So the **main assumption** is:** Seasonal effects are multiplicative.**

The other options are incorrect because:

 
• 
 
Random components are not assumed to dominate.

 
 
• 
 
The trend need not be constant.

 
 
• 
 
Additive seasonality is used in a different method (difference method)
